title: Pre-Analysis — Reinforcement of the Outboard Flap Track Fairing Attachment Rib

ata.title: Wing Trailing Edge — Flap Support Structure

abstract: Cancelled pre-analysis of the first bonded configuration of the flap track fairing attachment rib reinforcement at outboard track 3, closed when the design office withdrew the configuration in favour of a bolted rib.

sections.objective: Assess the first proposed configuration of the attachment rib reinforcement at outboard flap track 3, in which a bonded angle was to be added to the existing rib foot, and establish whether the published repair scheme for the fixed trailing edge panel could still be applied to a reinforced rib. The order was raised by the wing structures office after fairing attachment findings on high cycle aircraft, and was scoped to the outboard track region only.
sections.findings_summary: The analysis stopped after the first two findings. The published doubler repair at the fairing attachment land was found to occupy the fastener rows the bonded angle needs, and because the repair is applied at the same station on almost every aircraft with a fairing finding, the two would meet on the majority of the target fleet rather than occasionally. That result was reported to the design office before the remaining tasks were started. The office withdrew the bonded configuration within the week and re-cut the change as a bolted rib with a different footprint, at which point the work order no longer had a subject. A second, informational item on prior art for bonded reinforcement over an existing land was recorded before closure.
sections.next_steps: The work order was cancelled rather than revised, because the bolted configuration changes the footprint, the load path and the repair interaction and none of the completed work carries over. A fresh pre-analysis was raised against the bolted configuration. The two findings recorded here were handed to that order as a starting point, together with the fastener row survey that had already been completed for the outboard track region.

similarity_seeds: local reinforcement of a fairing attachment land
bonded angle added to an existing rib foot

tasks.title: Search published repairs at the fixed trailing edge fairing lands
Survey the fastener rows in the outboard track region
Assess flap control system clearance in the reinforced area

expected_findings.rationale: The published doubler repair at the fairing attachment land takes the fastener rows the bonded angle was to be laid over, and it is applied at the same station on almost every aircraft that has had a fairing finding. The two therefore meet on most of the target fleet, not occasionally, and the bonded angle cannot be qualified over a repaired land.
expected_findings.resolution: None taken on this configuration. The finding was transferred to the pre-analysis of the bolted rib, where the footprint moves outboard of the repair land.

evidence.similarity_note: Retrieved by similarity alone while searching for prior art on adding material over an existing load path. The lower shell external patch and the fairing rib angle share no identifier, no zone and no chapter, and the two texts have almost no vocabulary in common, but both describe the qualification argument for laying a stiff element over a fastened joint.

expected_findings.rationale: Recorded because the lower shell repair carries the only published bonding qualification argument on the type for a stiff element over a fastened joint, and the design office wanted it on file before it committed to a bonded configuration.
expected_findings.resolution: Handed to the follow-on pre-analysis as background; no action on either document.

type_data.conclusion: Cancelled 2016-11-22. The bonded configuration was rejected on the repair interaction before the analysis was complete; the design office re-cut the change as a bolted rib and a new work order was raised.
